turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Doctor: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today? Patient: I’ve noticed small, non-itchy bumps on my left thigh for about three weeks. I’ve also been feeling fatigued and generally unwell for a few months.
Doctor: Can you describe the appearance of the bumps—size, color, shape, and whether they have changed or spread since they first appeared?

Patient: They’re small bumps that look kind of skin-colored to slightly reddish, and they haven’t really changed much over the three weeks. They’ve stayed on the left thigh without spreading noticeably, and they aren’t itchy or painful.
Doctor: Besides the fatigue, have you noticed

Patient: I haven’t noticed fever, cough, or shortness of breath, and I don’t have any painful areas on the skin. I also haven’t had any weight loss or night sweats, and the bumps haven’t been getting worse or spreading.
Doctor: Are the bumps firm or soft
Patient: They feel a bit firm rather than soft, and they don’t hurt when I press them. They’re not tender, and they haven’t seemed to change in consistency over the past few weeks.
Doctor: Did you notice
Patient: I don’t think they’re draining anything, and I haven’t seen any blisters or ulcers. I’d say they’ve stayed pretty localized to that one area on my left thigh.
Doctor: Have you had any recent trauma, insect bites, or skin irritation to that part of your thigh before the bumps appeared?
Patient: I don’t recall any specific trauma or insect bites, and I haven’t had any new skin irritation, creams, or repeated friction on that spot before the bumps started.
Doctor: Approximately how large are the individual bumps—can you estimate their diameter in centimeters or millimeters?
Patient: They’re pretty small—about 2–4 millimeters across, roughly like the tip of a pencil eraser, and there are only a limited number clustered on my left thigh.
Doctor: Have you noticed any similar bumps or any other skin changes anywhere else on your body?
Patient: I haven’t noticed similar bumps anywhere else, and there haven’t been other skin changes besides that cluster on my left thigh.
Doctor: Have you noticed any swollen or tender lymph nodes anywhere on your body—especially in the groin, underarms, neck, or elsewhere?
Patient: I haven’t noticed any swollen or tender lymph nodes in my groin, underarms, or neck. I’m not feeling any lumps or pain in those areas.
Doctor: Have you started any new medications, supplements, or topical products in the past few months that might coincide with the onset of the bumps or your fatigue?
Patient: No—I haven’t started any new medications, supplements, or topical products in the past few months. I’m not using any creams on my skin, and nothing changed right before the bumps started.
Doctor: When you gently pinch the center of one of the bumps, does it create a small “dimple” or indentation in the skin?
Patient: I haven’t tried pinching the center closely enough to notice a dimple, but they seem to stay raised and firm rather than collapsing or showing any indentation.
Doctor: When you gently move one of the bumps with your fingertip, does it glide over the skin (mobile) or feel anchored to the deeper tissue (fixed)?
Patient: They feel pretty anchored, not like they glide freely over the skin. I don’t think they move much when I touch them gently.
Doctor: When you gently squeeze the sides of one of the bumps (the “dimple sign”), does the center of the lesion pull inward or create a small indentation?
Patient: I haven’t tried squeezing the center closely enough to see if it pulls inward, but when I look at them they seem raised and don’t create a visible indentation.
Doctor: Do any of the bumps have a tiny central pore or dark dot that looks like a punctum in the middle of the lesion?
Patient: I haven’t noticed any tiny central pore, dark dot, or punctum in the middle of the bumps. They look like small raised bumps with a skin-colored to slightly reddish tone.
Doctor: If you press a fingertip firmly against one of the bumps, does the redness or color fade (i.e., does it blanch) while you maintain pressure?

Patient: I haven’t specifically checked if the color fades when I press on them, but they don’t seem to change much in appearance with gentle pressure. I can say they look fairly fixed in color rather than transient.
[DDX] Dermatofibroma, Epidermal inclusion cyst, Granuloma annulare, Cutaneous sarcoidosis, Cutaneous involvement of lymphoma
